data.title: SRX Global Provides Update on Balance Sheet and Share Buyback
data.description:
NORTH PALM BEACH, Fla., Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SRX Global Inc. (NYSE American: SRXH) (the “Company” or “SRX”), an AI-enabled platform dedicated to generating long-term shareholder value through investments in high-conviction operating companies and strategic assets, today is providing shareholders with an update on its balance sheet and share buyback.

As of October 30, 2026, the Company has approximately $34 million in aggregate cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term U.S. Treasury bills. The Company does not have any exposure to cryptocurrency as of today. These balances are preliminary, unaudited, based on currently available information and subject to adjustment upon completion of applicable accounting and reconciliation procedures. They do not represent September 30, 2026 fiscal year-end balances or a complete presentation of the Company’s financial condition. The Company currently expects to report its fiscal year-end results and file its Annual Report on Form 10-K in early December 2026.

Additionally, the Company has been actively utilizing its stock repurchase program as of today’s release. The program permits repurchases of up to the lesser of 10 million shares or 50% of its issued and outstanding common stock at any given time, for an aggregate purchase price not exceeding $20 million, through July 7, 2027. Future repurchases are subject to market conditions, available capital and applicable legal requirements.

The Company expects to disclose the total number of shares repurchased and the average price paid for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 when it reports its fiscal year-end results in early December 2026.

About SRX Global Inc.
SRX Global is an AI-driven platform focused on generating long-term shareholder value through investments in high-conviction operating companies, strategic assets, and technology-enabled opportunities. The Company leverages proprietary technology, data analytics, and disciplined capital allocation to identify and manage investments across multiple sectors.

data.title: From Prison Classroom to National Audience: "Basement People" Screens at San Quentin Film Festival and Digitally Debuts Nationally on Securus Technologies Tablets
data.description:
From Prison Classroom to National Audience: "Basement People" Screens at San Quentin Film Festival and Digitally Debuts Nationally on Securus Technologies Tablets

From Prison Classroom to National Audience: "Basement People" Screens at San Quentin Film Festival and Digitally Debuts Nationally on Securus Technologies Tablets

PR Newswire

PLANO, Texas, Oct. 30, 2026

Directed by Christine Swanson and winner of Best Short Film at the Martha's Vineyard African American Film Festival, Kyale Akeem Williams' Academy Award-eligible film is now available to incarcerated viewers nationwide

PLANO, Texas, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Basement People, an Academy Award-eligible short film written by incarcerated screenwriter Kyale Akeem Williams and directed by award-winning filmmaker Christine Swanson, screens at the 2026 San Quentin Film Festival. Technology access inside correctional facilities carried the film from a Michigan prison classroom to the festival circuit and secure tablets nationwide, extending education beyond the classroom, sustaining creative collaboration, and building the connection, skills, and sense of purpose essential to rehabilitation.

On October 22, 2026, Securus Technologies, a technology company that equips more than 1,800 correctional agencies with a comprehensive portfolio of connectivity solutions that enhance public safety and optimize facility operations, made Basement People available to incarcerated viewers through the Securus Media Store. Delivered across Securus' network of more than 550,000 secure tablets in corrections facilities nationwide, the release expands access to meaningful content that can spark reflection, reinforce learning, and bring to life where education and creative work can lead in rehabilitation and reentry.

Williams developed the screenplay through a Calvin Prison Initiative screenwriting course at Michigan's Richard A. Handlon Correctional Facility. Recognizing the strength of his work, Calvin University professor Geert Heetebrij connected Williams with Swanson, a fellow Detroiter who went on to direct the film. Through JPay accounts on the Securus platform, Williams stayed connected with Swanson and the project's broader support network, allowing them to continue developing the screenplay during his incarceration and turn classroom learning into sustained creative collaboration.

"When I first read the script, I was struck by its emotional precision, moral ambiguity, and relatable characters," said Swanson, whose directing credits include The Clark Sisters: First Ladies of Gospel and Albany Road. "It did not ask for pity. It asked for understanding. Now, people inside may see their own families reflected in it, and that means a great deal to me."

The film follows Tina, a seven-year-old girl who retreats to her family's basement after a traumatic incident and finds refuge with her uncle Keith, whom the family has dismissed and isolated. Their bond creates safety without judgment and illustrates how empathy and connection can interrupt cycles of neglect and harm.

"I wrote Basement People to explore how vulnerable family members respond to familial violence, emotional abuse, and mental health conditions," said Williams. "I hope this interpersonal complexity will encourage audiences to sympathize with the protagonist without dehumanizing her tough and aggressive family. After all, each family member is a victim in their own way—someone who also deserves love, mercy, and compassion."

After winning Best Short Film at the Martha's Vineyard African American Film Festival, Basement People earned Academy Award eligibility. Its screening at the San Quentin Film Festival, now in its third year and the first film festival established inside a U.S. prison, brings a screenplay developed inside one correctional facility to an audience inside another, proving how education, creative opportunity, and technology access can carry work beyond institutional walls.

"Access to technology while incarcerated gives individuals an opportunity to discover and develop abilities they may never have had the chance to explore," said Jessica Lust, Chief Product Officer, Securus Technologies. "In particular, secure tablets create connectivity to educational tools, mentors, and collaborators that lead to skill building, motivation, and purpose, which can be the foundations of rehabilitation and successful reentry."

"Our responsibility extends beyond providing services. It includes listening to the communities where we operate and supporting the local people and organizations that understand what their communities need to thrive," said Shamia Lodge, Stakeholder Engagement Director, Securus Technologies. "When we pair their insight with resources that expand access and opportunity, we help create conditions in which more individuals can build lasting success."

About Securus Technologies
Securus Technologies, an Aventiv company and the industry leader, equips more than 1,800 correctional agencies with a comprehensive portfolio of technology solutions that enhance public safety and optimize facility operations. Securus helps agencies bring communications, intelligence, mobility, education, monitoring, and operational visibility together in one integrated ecosystem that improves safety, efficiency, and outcomes. Through purpose-built infrastructure, extensive corrections expertise, and continuous investment in innovation, Securus helps agencies modernize how corrections work while supporting successful reentry and stronger communities.

About Basement People
Basement People explores the impact of trauma poverty, and untreated mental illness on children and urban communities. Through Tina, a sensitive young girl, and her uncle Keith, a man isolated by his own struggles, the film reveals how cycles of neglect and violence can be interrupted by empathy and understanding.

Written by Kyale Akeem Williams, an incarcerated writer at Michigan's Richard A. Handlon Correctional Facility through the Calvin Prison Initiative and directed by award-winning filmmaker Christine Swanson, Basement People unites two artists whose shared roots ground the film in authenticity. This collaboration bridges art, justice and community healing while amplifying Detroit's creative legacy.

data.title: Tidal Wave Auto Spa Opens New Conveyor Car Wash in Merritt Island, Florida
data.description:
THOMASTON, GA / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / Tidal Wave Auto Spa®, one of the nation's largest conveyor car wash companies, is pleased to announce the grand opening of its newest conveyor car wash in Merritt Island, Florida. Now open at 55 S Banana River Drive, the new Merritt Island car wash marks the company's 33rd location in the Sunshine State and 339th nationwide.

To celebrate the Grand Opening, the Merritt Island location is offering 12 days of free premium car washes from October 28 to November 8. This limited-time promotion lets customers experience the company's premium wash option, Graph-X4® + Super Shammy, at no cost. The Merritt Island location features mat cleaning stations, complimentary tire air, spot-free rinse, undercarriage wash, foam and wax treatments, and tire shine - delivering a complete car care experience from start to finish. Tidal Wave is also extending its popular Founders Club offer through the Grand Opening celebration (October 28-November 8) - available on the top 3 wash plans, new members pay just $10 for their first month, then receive $10 off each month for the following 12 months, for 13 months of savings. New Tidal Wave members gain access to the entire 339-location networkspanning 30 states, offering unmatched convenience for customers on the go.

Tidal Wave is proud to invest in the communities it calls home, having donated more than $8.5 million to charitable organizations nationwide. In celebration of the Merritt Island grand opening, the company will host Giveback Day on Wednesday, November 4, from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., donating $1 for every free wash and $5 for every new Tidal Wave Clean Club membership to The Children's Hunger Project. Donations will support The Children's Hunger Project's mission to provide weekend food packages to elementary school children in need across Brevard County - ensuring kids have access to nourishing food when school meals are unavailable. What started with one school and 27 children has grown to serve nearly 5,000 children across 60 schools, addressing a critical gap in a county where 70% of public elementary school students qualify for free or reduced meals.

"Opening our 33rd location in Florida in Merritt Island is an exciting step for Tidal Wave, and we're excited to bring our premium car wash experience to the heart of the Space Coast. We're also proud to support The Children's Hunger Project through our Giveback Day and help children across Brevard County get the nourishing food they need. We look forward to serving this community and becoming a trusted part of it," said Tidal Wave Auto Spa CEO and Founder, Scott Blackstock.

Tidal Wave proudly serves customers at 339 conveyor car wash locations across the United States, including 33 in Florida, with additional Sunshine State openings planned this year in Wimauma.

With single wash options starting at $15, unlimited wash memberships and family plans, and fleet plans for businesses, Tidal Wave delivers solutions to fit every need.

data.title: HelloNation Article Featuring Dental Expert Dr. Calvin Despain Explains Dental Cleaning Frequency
data.description:
HelloNation Article Featuring Dental Expert Dr. Calvin Despain Explains Dental Cleaning Frequency

HelloNation Article Featuring Dental Expert Dr. Calvin Despain Explains Dental Cleaning Frequency

PR Newswire

MOSES LAKE, Wash., Oct. 30, 2026

The article outlines how often patients should schedule cleanings to support gum health and long-term oral health maintenance.

MOSES LAKE, Wash., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- How often should you get dental cleanings to maintain a healthy smile? The answer is explored in a HelloNation article featuring insights from Dental Expert Dr. Calvin Despain of Skyview Dental in Moses Lake, Washington.

The HelloNation article explains that dental cleaning frequency plays a central role in maintaining oral health. For many adults, visiting the dentist every six months is considered standard. This timing allows for consistent plaque and tartar removal before buildup can lead to more serious concerns. The article emphasizes that even with strong brushing and flossing habits, plaque can accumulate daily and eventually harden into tartar that requires professional dental cleanings.

According to the article, professional dental cleanings are designed to reach areas that routine home care may miss. These visits help reduce harmful bacteria and support long-term gum health. Dental Expert Dr. Calvin Despain is featured in the article, which highlights how regular Moses Lake dental cleaning appointments can make future visits easier and more comfortable by limiting buildup between appointments.

The article notes that while a six-month schedule works well for many, dental cleaning frequency varies for everyone. Some patients may benefit from more frequent visits, such as every three to four months. This is often recommended for individuals with a history of gum disease, heavy buildup, or health conditions that affect oral health. The article explains that personalized care plans help ensure effective gum disease prevention and better long-term outcomes.

Gum health is a key focus throughout the article. It describes how plaque and tartar removal helps prevent inflammation that can lead to gingivitis. If untreated, gingivitis may progress into more advanced gum disease, potentially affecting the bone that supports teeth. Regular professional dental cleanings reduce these risks and support healthier gums.

The HelloNation article also connects oral health maintenance with overall health. It explains that gum health has been linked to broader conditions such as heart disease and complications related to diabetes. By maintaining consistent dental cleanings in Moses Lake, patients can reduce inflammation and support both oral and general health.

Another important benefit discussed is early detection. The article explains how routine visits enable dental professionals to identify issues such as cavities and gum recession at an early stage. Addressing these concerns early often leads to simpler treatments and helps patients avoid more complex procedures later. Dental Expert Dr. Calvin Despain is included in the article as a source of insight on how consistent monitoring supports effective gum disease prevention.

The article further explains that maintaining a steady dental cleaning frequency improves patient comfort over time. With less plaque and tartar buildup, appointments tend to be quicker and more predictable. This consistency encourages patients to stay on track with their oral health maintenance routines and reinforces the importance of regular care.

For residents seeking guidance, the article emphasizes that the right schedule depends on individual needs. Factors such as medical history, lifestyle habits, and current gum condition all play a role. A personalized approach ensures that professional dental cleanings remain effective and aligned with each patient's oral health goals.

How Often Should You Get Dental Cleanings in Moses Lake? features insights from Dr. Calvin Despain, Dental Expert at Skyview Dental in Moses Lake, Washington, on HelloNation.

About HelloNation

HelloNation is America's Good News Network, a premier media platform built on the idea that good news travels faster when real people tell real stories. Through its community-focused publications and innovative "edvertising" approach, HelloNation delivers content that informs, inspires, and spotlights the leaders making a meaningful impact in their communities.

data.title: From Fairways to Futures: Swings for STEM Raises $100,000
data.description:
From Fairways to Futures: Swings for STEM Raises $100,000

From Fairways to Futures: Swings for STEM Raises $100,000

PR Newswire

WASHINGTON, Oct. 30, 2026

Third Annual Event Brings Together Chemical Industry Leaders, Policymakers, Academic Partners and Students to Strengthen Tomorrow's Workforce

WASHINGTON, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Alliance for Chemical Distribution (ACD) and American Chemistry Council (ACC) joined forces Monday for the third annual Swings for STEM golf tournament, raising $100,000 to support the next generation of scientists, engineers, and innovators. The event brought together stakeholders from industry, government and academia for a day of friendly competition and fundraising benefiting the Future of STEM Scholars Initiative (FOSSI) and Creating Exciting Futures in STEM (CEFinSTEM) , two organizations that seek to inspire, support, and expand access to STEM education.

"The future of our industry depends on the next generation of scientists, engineers, and innovators, and we have a responsibility to help them succeed," said Eric R. Byer, President and CEO of ACD. "Swings for STEM is about more than raising money. It's about opening doors, building relationships, and giving talented young people the opportunity to see what's possible in the chemical distribution industry. We're incredibly grateful to our sponsors, donors, and participants for helping us invest in the next generation of STEM leaders."

"Chemistry is at the heart of American innovation, and maintaining that leadership starts with investing in the next generation," added Chris Jahn, President and CEO of the American Chemistry Council. "When we launched FOSSI, our goal was to create new pathways into STEM careers and strengthen the chemical industry's talent pipeline. Today, more than 900 scholarships have been funded through that effort. Swings for STEM reflects that same vision, bringing industry and policy partners together to raise nearly $300,000 over the past three years."

The event also featured a dedicated student program for FOSSI scholars, combining a golf clinic, leadership development workshop, and networking opportunities.

FOSSI Scholar Brandon Simmons was one of nearly 20 scholarship recipients who attended the event, sharing, "My experience at Swings for STEM was truly rewarding. I enjoyed learning new techniques and connecting with fellow FOSSI scholars from different schools. The event was a great opportunity to build relationships, share experiences, and grow alongside other scholars. I'm grateful to FOSSI for creating opportunities like this that foster both personal growth and a strong sense of community."

To learn more about FOSSI visit www.FutureofSTEMScholars.org. Scholarship applications are open until January 8th, 2027. Eligible students can apply here.

To learn more about CEFinSTEM, visit www.cefinstem.org.

data.title: Is your crypto safe? What Binance's $6.3 billion hack means for bitcoin investors.
data.description:
By Isabel Wang and Joseph Adinolfi

A look at how safe your money really is when even the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange can be breached

Bitcoin and related stocks tumbled Friday after a record hack of the cryptocurrency platform Binance

A record $6.3 billion hack of Binance has put one of the crypto world's oldest risks back in the spotlight: How safe is investors' money when even the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange can be breached?

Prices of bitcoin and Ethereum were tumbling on Friday after Binance disclosed the hack - described as the largest relating to cryptocurrencies on record - that raises new concerns about whether investors can count on crypto exchanges to keep their assets safe.

Bitcoin (BTCUSD) was down 2.3% at $76,846 a coin in recent trading, while Ethereum (ETHUSD) was 1.2% lower, at $2,227, according to FactSet data.

Binance promised to cover all customer losses, and vowed to restart withdrawals within two days after freezing them as a security precaution. By working with industry partners, the exchange also managed to freeze about $3 billion in stolen assets, and the company has already started the recovery process, a Binance spokesperson told MarketWatch.

Nonetheless, the hack underscores a persistent challenge facing the cryptocurrency industry: convincing investors that their assets are safe in an ecosystem that continues to be plagued by security breaches.

"With certainty, we [investors] do have an inaccurate assessment of what occurred and the losses that happened in the market," said Ryan Kirkley, co-founder and CEO at Global Settlement Network Institutional, a blockchain infrastructure firm. "Bitcoin is not recoverable."

In another statement to MarketWatch, Binance said it has already reserved over $6.34 billion of company funds to cover this incident, while $5 billion of these funds are already held in the exact token assets that were impacted. They are also completing the purchase of the remaining amount by buying token assets through market channels and over-the-counter channels, which may take longer, according to a Binance spokesperson.

Cybersecurity research firm TRM Labs said the attacker, which it identified as TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean hacking unit, converted a large portion of the stolen funds into assets that are beyond any issuer's ability to claw them back.

In other words, promising depositors that "everything is under control" ignores the irreversible nature of blockchain transactions, Kirkley told MarketWatch via phone on Friday.

Putting money into the crypto market through an exchange is fundamentally different from investing in traditional, regulated markets, such as stocks and bonds. If your stockbroker goes bankrupt or fraud occurs, the Securities Investor Protection Corporation can protect your portfolio up to $500,000. However, crypto custodians, exchanges, brokers, wallet providers and neobanks often don't carry federal deposit insurance.

"Binance's ability to swallow what will be 5% of their entire holdings is remarkable, if they're able to do it, but to say they're able to do it without there being downstream sales and liquidations will be a very unlikely thing to happen," Kirkley added.

"We're talking about the world's largest crypto exchange relying on emergency freezes and reimbursement promises to contain a multibillion-dollar incident. That's a serious problem for an industry asking institutions to trust it with substantially more capital," Kirkley said.

The Binance hack isn't the only notable security incident to hit the crypto industry lately. Just last month, Bitget said that crypto worth roughly $350 million had been stolen from the platform, while a record $1.5 billion worth of Ethereum was stolen from the exchange Bybit early last year.

The onus is now on exchanges to prove customers' funds are secure. That's why until there is greater clarity around how this hack occurred, it is reasonable for investors to reassess how much capital they need to keep on the platform versus what can be held elsewhere, said Sean Farrell, head of digital asset strategy at Fundstrat.

Shares of crypto-related stocks were under pressure on Friday. Strategy (MSTR), Circle Internet Group (CRCL) and Coinbase (COIN) were all falling at least 9%, while shares of Robinhood (HOOD) were off nearly 10%, according to FactSet data.

Separately, Polymarket temporarily halted trading on its international platform Thursday after hackers exploited an engineering flaw to drain between $2.5 million and $2.7 million from over 700 users' wallets. Polymarket has a data partnership with Dow Jones, the publisher of MarketWatch.

Hacks across the crypto industry have further dampened investor appetite for the once-popular risk asset. It has struggled in October after a late-summer rally brought bitcoin's price back above $70,000 for the first time in about three months. A number of other factors had been weighing on sentiment in the market, including expectations for more Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes in 2026, as well as fears that the voracious artificial-intelligence spending spree might not pay off.

data.title: Dover Announces Upsize of Its Tender Cap and Extension of Expiration Date of Previously Announced Offer to Purchase for Cash Certain of Its Outstanding Debt Securities
data.description:
DOWNERS GROVE, Ill., Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Dover (NYSE: DOV), a diversified global manufacturer, today announced that it has amended its previously announced cash tender offers (the “Tender Offers”) to purchase the outstanding notes described below, by increasing the tender cap from an aggregate purchase price of $230,000,000 to $300,000,000 (the “Tender Cap”). Dover also announced that it will extend the Expiration Date of the Tender Offers. The Tender Offers are being made upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Offer to Purchase dated October 26, 2026 (the “Offer to Purchase”).

The Expiration Date for the Tender Offers has been extended to 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 5, 2026, unless further extended or earlier terminated by Dover with respect to any Tender Offer. Tenders of Notes of a Series may be validly withdrawn at any time at or prior to 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 5, 2026, but, except as provided in the Offer to Purchase or required by applicable law, may not be validly withdrawn thereafter. The Price Determination Date (as defined below) has correspondingly been extended to 3:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 5, 2026.

The “Settlement Date” will be the second business day after the Expiration Date and is expected to be November 9, 2026.

The Notes offered to be purchased in the Tender Offers, in the order of acceptance priority, are the 6.650% Debentures due 2028; 6.600% Notes due 2038; 5.375% Debentures due 2035; and 5.375% Notes due 2041 (collectively, the “Notes”) for the consideration described below, up to the Tender Cap, subject to proration and the application of the Acceptance Priority Levels set forth in the table below and as further set forth in the Offer to Purchase. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this press release have the meanings given to them in the Offer to Purchase.

As of 12:30 p.m., New York City time, on October 30, 2026, approximately 28.86% of the aggregate principal amount of the 2028 Debentures, approximately 30.59% of the aggregate principal amount of the 2038 Notes, approximately 39.78% of the aggregate principal amount of the 2035 Debentures and approximately 30.83% of the aggregate principal amount of the 2041 Notes have been validly tendered in the applicable Tender Offers. Subject to applicable law, Dover may, but is under no obligation to, eliminate, further increase or decrease the Tender Cap at any time prior to the Expiration Date. In the event proration is required with respect to a Series of Notes, Dover will multiply the principal amount of each valid tender of such Series of Notes by the applicable proration rate and round the resulting amount down to the nearest integral multiple of the respective minimum denomination, in order to determine the principal amount of such tender that will be accepted pursuant to the applicable Tender Offer. The excess principal amount of Notes not accepted from the tendering Holders will be promptly returned to such Holders, and if this excess principal amount of Notes is less than the respective minimum denomination of such Series of Notes, Dover may either accept or reject all such tendering Holders’ validly tendered Notes in its sole discretion. Additionally, Dover may, but is under no obligation to, accept for purchase additional Notes of any Series in an aggregate principal amount not exceeding 2% of the outstanding aggregate principal amount of such Series without amending or extending the applicable Tender Offer, subject to applicable law, as further described in the Offer to Purchase, and may also further increase or decrease the percentage of the Notes accepted for payment in the Tender Offers (including by more than 2% of the outstanding aggregate principal amount of the Notes of the applicable Series) by a press release or other public announcement that is widely disseminated by no later than 9:00 a.m. (New York City time) on the third business day before the Expiration Date.

The “Total Consideration” for each Series of Notes payable per each $1,000 principal amount of such Series of Notes validly tendered for purchase will be based on the applicable Fixed Spread for such Series of Notes, plus the Reference Yield based on the bid-side price of the applicable Reference Security as quoted on the applicable Bloomberg Reference Page as of 3:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 5, 2026, unless further extended by Dover with respect to the applicable Tender Offer (such date and time with respect to a Tender Offer, as the same may be extended by Dover with respect to such Tender Offer, the “Price Determination Date”). Unless extended with respect to any Tender Offer, promptly after the Price Determination Date, Dover will announce in a press release, among other things, the Offer Yield and Total Consideration applicable to each Series of Notes accepted for purchase. In addition to the applicable Total Consideration, Holders whose Notes are accepted for purchase pursuant to a Tender Offer will receive accrued and unpaid interest on those Notes from the last interest payment date with respect to those Notes to, but excluding, the Settlement Date (the “Accrued Interest,” and the payment thereof, the “Accrued Coupon Payment”).

The Tender Offers are subject to certain conditions as described in the Offer to Purchase, including the Financing Condition, which requires that Dover shall have completed an offering (the “New Notes Offering”) of a new series of senior unsecured notes on terms and conditions satisfactory to Dover that results in its receipt of net proceeds that are sufficient to repay its €600,000,000 1.25% notes due 2026 at maturity. The New Notes Offering is expected to close on November 2, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.

In no event will the information contained in this press release regarding the New Notes Offering constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any new notes. If any condition is not satisfied, Dover is not obligated to accept for payment, purchase or pay for, and may delay the acceptance for payment of, any tendered Notes, in each case subject to applicable law, and may terminate or alter any or all of the Tender Offers. The Tender Offers are not contingent upon the tender of any aggregate minimum principal amount of Notes of any Series (subject to minimum denomination requirements as set forth in the Offer to Purchase), and none of the Tender Offers is conditioned on the consummation of any of the other Tender Offers.

Dover has retained Deutsche Bank Securities Inc., HSBC Securities (USA) Inc. and J.P. Morgan Securities LLC to act as dealer managers (the “Dealer Managers”) for the Tender Offers. D.F. King & Co., Inc. will act as the Tender and Information Agent for the Tender Offers. Copies of the Offer to Purchase are available at www.dfking.com/dover. You may also contact your broker, dealer, commercial bank, trust company or other nominee for assistance concerning the Tender Offers.

Holders of Notes are advised to check with each bank, securities broker or other intermediary through which they hold Notes as to when such intermediary would need to receive instructions from a beneficial owner in order for that beneficial owner to be able to participate in, or withdraw their instruction to participate in, the Tender Offers before the deadlines specified herein and in the Offer to Purchase. The deadlines set by any such intermediary and DTC for the submission and withdrawal of tender instructions may be earlier than the relevant deadlines specified herein and in the Offer to Purchase.

This press release is neither an offer to purchase nor a solicitation of an offer to sell the Notes or any other securities. The Tender Offers are made only by and pursuant to the terms of the Offer to Purchase and only to such persons and in such jurisdictions as is permitted under applicable law. The information in this press release is qualified by reference to the Offer to Purchase. None of Dover, the Dealer Managers, the Tender and Information Agent or the trustee for each Series of the Notes makes any recommendation as to whether Holders should tender their Notes pursuant to the Tender Offers. Holders must make their own decisions as to whether to tender Notes, and, if so, the principal amount of Notes to tender.

Forward-Looking Statements

This press release includes forward-looking statements, including with respect to the Tender Offers and the New Notes Offering. Forward-looking statements are subject to known and unknown risks and uncertainties, including general economic conditions, supply chain constraints, inflation in material input costs, changes in customer demand, competitive factors, changes in law, the impact of interest rate and currency exchange rate fluctuations, and various other factors described in Dover’s periodic reports filed with or furnished to the Securities and Exchange Commission. These forward-looking statements speak only as of the date on which such statements were made, and Dover undertakes no obligation to update or revise these statements, except as required by federal securities laws.

About Dover:

Dover is a diversified global manufacturer and solutions provider with annual revenue of over $8 billion. We deliver innovative equipment and components, consumable supplies, aftermarket parts, software and digital solutions, and support services through five operating segments: Engineered Products, Clean Energy & Fueling, Imaging & Identification, Pumps & Process Solutions and Climate & Sustainability Technologies. Dover combines global scale with operational agility to lead the markets we serve. Recognized for our entrepreneurial approach for over 70 years, our team of approximately 24,000 employees takes an ownership mindset, collaborating with customers to redefine what’s possible. Headquartered in Downers Grove, Illinois, Dover trades on the New York Stock Exchange under “DOV.”
